subject: Hosted API pilot sizing & pricing — Halcyon Health
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@halcyon.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pilot sizing & pricing — Halcyon Health

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can move toward a pilot quote: 

Key signals from call:
- Expected steady-state: ~18M tokens/month across inference (mix of short prompts + 600-token outputs).
- Peak window: up to ~1,200 TPS sustained for 3–5 minute bursts during batch notification runs (99th percentile spikes).
- Target $/1M: Halcyon mentioned a target in the ~$12–18/1M ballpark, but said final decision depends on SLO guarantees and burst handling.

Immediate asks:
1) Could you confirm the 18M/month steady estimate and whether the 1,200 TPS peak is an upper bound or a frequent occurrence?
2) Any procurement timelines or pilot acceptance criteria we should know about (SLA, data residency, SOC2 evidence)?

Attached: your usage snapshot and the initial pricing table so you can see rough bands. I’ll loop in Karthik and Jordan to propose a pilot pricing approach that balances unit economics with your burst requirements.

Next steps: if numbers above are correct, I’ll propose a two-week pilot configuration (dedicated hosted pool + auto-fallback to lower-cost model for overflow) and a draft mutual action plan.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachment: halcyon_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)
Attachment: redwood_pricing_table_v2.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@halcyon.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@halcyon.com
Date: 2025-10-05T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot sizing & pricing — Halcyon Health

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the recap. Confirming the estimates:
- 18M/month is our midpoint expectation for alpha (could be +/- 25% depending on adoption).
- Peak: 1,200 TPS is our planning upper bound; more realistically we see ~700–900 TPS for 90% of spikes, but up to 1,200 when multiple customer events coincide.

Procurement notes:
- We typically ask for a 30-day pilot with clear measurables (latency p95/p99, request success rate).
- SOC2 + basic data processing addendum is required; procurement@halcyon.com will drive the paper.

For pricing: the $12–18/1M target is what our finance team prefers — if you can show a path to the lower end for steady state with controlled surges, that will make internal approval easier.

Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to confirm pilot criteria.

— Alex
Alex Zhou
Product Lead, Integrations | Halcyon Health
alex.zhou@halcyon.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@halcyon.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, procurement@halcyon.com
Date: 2025-10-05T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot sizing & pricing — Halcyon Health

Appreciate the clarification, Alex — that helps. Quick proposal (high level) to align with your procurement ask and your $/1M target: 

Pilot proposal (30 days):
- Steady band pricing: $14/1M tokens for usage between 10M–25M tokens/month (we can price step-downs after commitment review).
- Burst protection: included burst allowance up to 1,000 TPS with an overage mechanism for spikes above 1,000 TPS priced at a premium rate (this avoids needing reserved capacity for very short events).
- SLOs: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for the pilot pool; 99.9% availability target for API endpoints.
- Observability: per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, and prefix cache hit-rate exported to your metrics during the pilot.

If you confirm a firm commitment to 18M/month steady (or a 25% +/- window), we can offer a one-time pilot credit to effectively bring the first-month unit rate to $12/1M as a commercial concession, subject to an agreement on runbook and acceptance criteria.

I’ve attached an updated pricing table with the banded rates and the pilot credit example. If that looks reasonable I’ll draft a short MSA addendum and the mutual action plan.

Would you and procurement be available for a 20-min call tomorrow at 10:30am PT?

Thanks,
Naomi
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Halcyon pilot pricing note

Naomi / Jordan — quick internal note before the call with Halcyon. Key points to take: 

1) Margin check: at $14/1M steady for 18M tokens, unit economics are OK if we:
   - Use mixed model routing (higher-capacity open model for burst overflow)
   - Enable prefix caching and reduce average output length where feasible
2) Burst handling: offering 1,000 TPS included is defensible if we cap contiguous burst billing to minutes and route overflow to a cost-optimized fallback. Document the rollback plan in the MAP.
3) Contract ask: make the pilot credit contingent on a short acceptance test (3-day latency & success window) to limit exposure.

Action items for call:
- Naomi: confirm pilot acceptance criteria and ownership.
- Jordan: prep a one-page runbook + telemetry checklist to send post-call.
- Karthik: I’ll draft the price band note and the conditional pilot credit language.

-Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
